Q: How to run 2 commands at once, in parallel, auto-executing each command in a pane. For PowerShell but looking for a cross-platform terminal workflow A:

Honestly, you're running into the classic "PowerShell isn't a Unix shell" friction. I dev across Windows and Linux daily and just use the same workflow everywhere: tmux. On Windows, you can run tmux inside WSL2 or Git Bash, and it works identically to Linux/macOS.

If you want a pure Windows Terminal solution that opens panes side-by-side, the magic incantation is this:

wt -M new-tab ; split-pane -H ; move-focus left ; new-tab ; move-focus right

But that's clunky. Instead, just create a Windows Terminal profile that launches with a custom command line:

  1. Open Windows Terminal settings Ctrl+,

  2. Add a new profile with this command:

wt new-tab --title "Program 1" powershell -NoExit -Command "C:\path\to\program_1.exe" ; split-pane -H --title "Program 2" powershell -NoExit -Command "python C:\path\to\program_2.py"

That'll open one window with two panes, each running its own thing. Not exactly "one command from the existing shell" but you can trigger it with wt -p "MyProfileName".

For a truly cross-platform approach, I'd ditch PowerShell for the launcher and use a Makefile or justfile with a target like:

dev:
    tmux new-session -d -s mysession 'cd /path/to/project && python program2.py'
    tmux split-window -h 'cd /path/to/project && ./program1'
    tmux attach -t mysession

On Windows with WSL2 or Git Bash, that just works. On Linux/macOS, same thing. Zero mental overhead switching OSes.

If you're stuck on native Windows without WSL, you could also use concurrently(Node.js) or write a tiny Python script that uses subprocess.Popen for each command, but that won't give you separate panes, just parallel execution in the same output.

I used to fight with PowerShell jobs and ForEach-Object -Parallel, but honestly for long-running dev servers or watchers, the pane-based approach with tmux or wt profiles is way less headache.

Q: How do I get the module instance for a class in Python? A:

I would like to obtain the __path__ for the __module__ for self (which in this case will be the subclass). Problem is, __module__ returns a str rather than the module instance itself

For this task you need the sys module to get the module object by it's name.
The following code demonstrates how you can achieve this:


import sys

class Test:
    ...

# Create an instance (equals self)
instance = Test()
# Get the class of this instance
class_of_instance = type(instance)
# Proof that it is the class of the instance
print(class_of_instance == instance.__class__)
# Get module name of class
name_of_module_class_was_defined_in = class_of_instance.__module__
# Proof it is the same module
print(__name__ == name_of_module_class_was_defined_in)
# Get the module-object
module_object = sys.modules[__name__]

Q: Why am I getting this: [SystemGestureGate] <0x102210320> Gesture: System gesture gate timed out A:

I was getting this error, and no gestures were working in top area on my screen. It was some dropdown that had pointer events none with React Native not allowing gestures to work in that area. Was a weird to discover the bug but some people also reported this happening in certain areas of their screen so that hinted me to the solution.

Q: Linux(Ubuntu) vscode postgress Loading cvs file - Premmision denied for opening file A:

for local stuff use \copy company_dim FROM '/home/henka/Desktop/sql_tut1/csv_files/company_dim.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true); from within the psql shell, this will run the command under your OS's user

COPY executes as the postgres user. if you really need COPY, the quickest workaround is to move the CSV file into a directory PostgreSQL already has access to like /tmp: cp /home/henka/Desktop/sql_tut1/csv_files/company_dim.csv /tmp/company_dim.csv

otherwise you'd need to do chmod o+x on each directory & subdirectory, i.e. on /home, one /home/henka etc, but i'd not do this because then your home directory is not so secure -- probably not a major concern, but not necessary
